chapter: Ma Rainey and the Palace Theater
title: Step 'n Fetchit offers her a job
summary: Step 'n Fetchit, scouting talent, used her as pianist in Lake Charles and offered $65 a week, but her parents refused.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Really, yes. Did you have any other encounters, or work with anybody else that was well known?

Well, I remember one time Step 'n Fetchit, who you know who he was, the old comedian, Step 'n Fetchit came through Louisiana, and he was sort of a scout, he was scouting around for talent for the studios, you know. He was quite a big man at that time. He was, you know, he was the thing. And he came through Lake Charles and they were looking for talent. And I think I had to play with that group also. I played with the little band that he had with him. They didn't have a piano, they needed a piano player or something, but anyway, I became involved with that, and they wanted me to stay with them. They wanted me to go to New Orleans with them and play a couple of other dates with them, and my folks said no way. My dad says, 'No, no, no. We can't let her. She
can't leave here." Said, "We can't let her go." So he offered me $65.00, I think, $65.00 a week or something like that. "We'll pay her $65.00 a week," he says. They wouldn't. They wouldn't let me.
Well, what kind of an act did Step have? Was it comedy? Was there music?

I think it was a revue, something like a little revue, but really what he was doing was sort of scouting around, you know, he was sort of scouting around. At this particular theater, the Palace Theater, where they used to have, as I say, shows, you know. They used to have vaudeville and different revues would come through, and this was what he was doing. He had a show with him. I can't remember now exactly, but it was a little variety show, and he of course was the star of the show, see, but he was going through Louisiana and into Texas and in through the south, and he was really sort of scouting and looking for talent also.
